questions.stem: In machine learning modelling, what is a Feature?
options: A new table created and populated from raw data using data wrangling, used as the source for an ML model
A button in a dashboard that runs a model
The algorithm that a data scientist chooses
The prediction produced by a model
A licence option in a data science tool
questions.explanation: A Feature is a new table, created and populated from raw data through data wrangling, that serves as the source data for a machine learning model.

questions.stem: How does I Am Datapedia! summarise what a Feature is in its key phrase?
options: A Feature is a trained model
A Feature is a data scientist's hypothesis
A Feature is nothing more than a traditional table
A Feature is a chart of raw data
A Feature is an unstructured document
questions.explanation: The author's key phrase is that a Feature is nothing more than a traditional table.

questions.stem: Why do data scientists need raw but relevant data rather than all raw data?
options: Because raw data is always encrypted
Because ML models cannot read tables
Because raw data is stored only on paper
Because raw data must be deleted after use
Because raw data includes irrelevant data, and training a model does not need all of it
questions.explanation: Raw data means irrelevant data as well, and in Big Data the sizes are huge, so only the relevant raw data is needed to train models.

questions.stem: Who ideally cleans and filters the data before it is fed into a machine learning model?
options: The end customers
Data engineers, or the data scientists themselves
The database vendor
The marketing department
The model itself
questions.explanation: Data scientists themselves, or ideally data engineers, clean and filter the data through data wrangling before feeding it to ML models.

questions.stem: A global table holds one million customer rows, but a model must predict buying behaviour for one country and one set of products. What is created?
options: A copy of the full one million rows
A random sample of one hundred rows
A second model for every other country
A new table holding only that country's data for the required products, used as the model's source
A summary report for management
questions.explanation: Rather than feeding all one million rows to the model, a Feature table is created containing only data for that country and product set, and it becomes the source for the ML model.

questions.stem: Which process is used to populate a Feature table from raw data?
options: Data Encryption
Data Archiving
Data Wrangling
Data Monetisation
Data Splitting
questions.explanation: The Feature table is created and populated from raw data using data wrangling, the cleaning and filtering done before data reaches the model.

questions.stem: How is Data Science described in the discussion of Feature tables?
options: Running algorithms and machine learning models on structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets for analytics
Designing relational databases for transactions
Writing reports for senior management
Backing up data to the cloud
Managing user access to data
questions.explanation: Data Science is described as running algorithms and ML models on structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets for analytics.

questions.stem: Which statement about a Feature table is NOT correct?
options: It is a table created from raw data
It is used as the source for a machine learning model
It is populated using data wrangling
It holds only the relevant raw data
It must contain all of the raw data available
questions.explanation: A Feature keeps only the raw data that is relevant to the model; one does not need all the raw data to train a model.

questions.stem: According to I Am Datapedia!, which group might not be aware of the term Feature as used in Data Science?
options: Data engineers
Non-data scientists and non-data citizens
Machine learning researchers
Database designers
ETL developers
questions.explanation: The author notes that non-data scientists or non-data citizens might not be aware of the term Feature.

questions.stem: What is described as the basic requirement of any machine learning model?
options: A cloud subscription
A graphical user interface
A dedicated data scientist per model
Data
A relational database licence
questions.explanation: For any ML model there is a basic requirement of data, and data scientists need raw but relevant raw data to work with.
